items.title: Hundreds of ships cross the Strait of Hormuz and some are going 'dark' to do it
items.description: Amid new strikes, the future of the Strait of Hormuz has again been plunged into uncertainty, but ships are finding a way through.

items.title: Netanyahu looks to be pushing Trump to his limits
items.description: The US president is in deepening trouble and he does not seem to know how to get himself out of it.

items.title: Property and the budget ease pressure on the RBA
items.description: With two Australian banks cutting fixed home loan rates, there is a ray of hope that the cycle of interest rate hikes has peaked and borrowing costs may be lower down the track — another sign the pace of economic change has moved into overdrive.

items.title: We were happier during the COVID-19 pandemic. The reason is money
items.description: Australians felt a greater sense of satisfaction during the COVID-19 pandemic than they do today, according to government data, when households are grappling with the impact of inflation, rising interest rates and a reduction in real wages.

items.title: Live: David Pocock demands Labor ensures 'fair return' from AI data centres
items.description: Independent senator David Pocock says the government needs to ensure a "fair return" for investment in artificial intelligence data centres. Follow live.

items.title: Young couple told by agent that landlords would not rent to 'people like you'
items.description: Hopeful renters say negative stereotypes about young people are making it almost impossible to secure a rental on the Sunshine Coast.

items.title: ICC chief prosecutor suspended after probe into sex abuse claims
items.description: The International Criminal Court's chief prosecutor, Karim Khan, has been suspended pending a vote by member states on his fate, following a probe into accusations of sexual harassment made against him.

items.title: The Taiwan crisis nobody is watching
items.description: Taipei sits at the physical centre of the global AI economy but remains shut out of the diplomatic rooms where its sovereign rights are negotiated, often by others.

items.title: Family's 'worst nightmare' after purchasing home filled with defects
items.description: After a young family invests their life savings in their dream home, only to discover it is filled with defects, SA's consumer watchdog issues a public warning notice about the builder responsible and seven other traders.

items.title: Live: Wall Street rebounds after semiconductor rout, OpenAI files to list
items.description: Wall Street is rebounding after a semiconductor rout, as artificial intelligence giant OpenAI files to become a public company. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Evans's coming out took extraordinary courage and the NRL must match it
items.description: Kane Evans showed remarkable bravery to reveal his sexuality to the world and now rugby league must lift to his level.

items.title: Four-time veterans to late bolters, here's your Socceroos pocket guide
items.description: Mat Ryan and Mathew Leckie are at a record-equalling fourth FIFA World Cup, while Cristian Volpato headlines a host of first-timers, after his late switch from Italy. Here's your complete guide to the Socceroos' World Cup squad.

items.title: NT youth mental health inpatient facility lacking basic safety standards
items.description: The Northern Territory's only youth mental health inpatient ward failed to meet 16 national safety standards, documents obtained under Freedom of Information laws have revealed.

items.title: Politically connected company won $15m government contract despite 'red flags'
items.description: A cybersecurity company with financial red flags received a $15m state contract in the dying days of the Miles government.

items.title: The criticism Marc Fennell always gets for Stuff the British Stole
items.description: Two years in the making, the Walkley Award-winning journalist is back with the third season of his globe-trotting historical mystery series. He's treating it like it's the last.

items.title: A straight woman steals a young gay man's story in Josh Silver's debut novel
items.description: Described as one of the books of the year, Fruit Fly asks who has the right to tell which stories in an age of cancellation for cultural appropriation.

items.title: Kings and Queens quiz: Where is Prince Harry in the royal line of succession?
items.description: The latest ABC More or Less quiz challenges you to rank some of the most famous (and infamous) royals in history, and sort some of the current crop.

items.title: Healthy people in hospitals are costing millions every day
items.description: As many medically well patients wait in public hospitals for a spot in aged care, their bodies begin to deteriorate at a rate experts believe is preventable.

items.title: $3,000 murder contracts and 'violence brokers' fuelling underworld bloodshed
items.description: One of the state's top police officers has promised feuding gangs bringing terror to Sydney's streets will not exist "by the time we finish" as police stare down a new era of disorganised crime.

items.title: Proposed NDIS changes and expectations for parents explained
items.description: Politicians are presiding over three days of public hearings into a bill paving the way for the biggest ever cuts to the NDIS.

items.title: 'Extremely traumatising': Modern slavery victims let down by police, courts
items.description: A new national report prepared for the office of the Australian anti-slavery commissioner finds modern slavery victims are being let down by the justice system.

items.title: Fire insiders raise alarm about Melbourne's data centre expansion
items.description: Serious concerns about an influx of large-scale data centres in Melbourne's west are being raised by Fire Rescue Victoria insiders.

items.title: Nate thought nobody would celebrate his 10th birthday. He was wrong
items.description: A mother's plea on social media turns into a community-wide extravaganza for her 10-year-old son.

items.title: Smut disease threatened to destroy sugarcane farming but ended up reshaping it
items.description: Twenty years ago, a Queensland farm became ground zero for a disease the sugarcane industry was dreading. Instead of destroying the industry, the response quietly transformed the state's biosecurity and farming practices.

items.title: Richard Scolyer remembered by peers for contributions to cancer treatment
items.description: Before being diagnosed with cancer, the 2024 Australian of the Year was a leading melanoma researcher, developing better therapies for those with the disease.
